answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a bond that only grows as it completes verified work, like a lotus rising through murky water on a single stem. An attacker crossing the ridge of that cost faces a simple trade - spawning a thousand fresh identities means locking a thousand bonds, while honest agents reuse one history. Sybil volume collapses when each new face must pay the same entry price as a real one.
